content.comment_body: Hello, I've created a program using [product_name] to control motors and solenoids based on set time intervals. The simulation runs without issues, and I've transferred it to the controller, switched it to run mode. However, turning on input I1 doesn’t power the outputs, though I hear the device switching. The input signal checks out fine. This is my first attempt at wiring a controller—please review the attached image. Am I making a wiring error?
Please refer to the attached image of the program.

Your wiring setup isn’t correct; the outputs on your [product_name] use relay contacts. Connect one side of the contact to the power supply’s positive terminal, and the other side to the coil. The coil’s negative terminal should go to the power supply’s negative. Regards, [user_name]
The outputs of [product_name] aren’t a power source—they work as switches.

You need to treat the outputs of [product_name] as switches and also take into account the contact’s maximum current rating. Don’t connect loads that exceed this; otherwise, the contact will get damaged. It’s best to connect a relay to the output contact and use it to drive the load.
Thanks, after changing the wiring, everything is functioning correctly.

Glad to hear it worked for you. Hopefully this was just for testing. When you move forward, make sure to use the correct connectors and wire colors for your coils, or there’s a risk of damaging your project in the future. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced difficulties wiring a [product_name] controller after a successful simulation using [product_name] programming software. The core issue was misunderstanding the output function—the user expected outputs to supply power rather than act as switches. Community responses clarified proper wiring and emphasized correct handling of relay contacts, helping the user fix the problem. This thread highlights a common novice mistake regarding controller output wiring and the need for clear guidance and documentation for beginners.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipated that controller outputs would directly power devices after uploading and running the program, expecting hardware connections to reflect simulation results without complications.
